text:
maya: Quick sync — runtime affordance + credential handoffs between hosted / dedicated / private. I think we missed a couple of edgecases after last week's RFC and the canary logs.

sam: Two quick things I noticed while reviewing logs: 1) ephemeral KMS tokens when bouncing from hosted->private paths; 2) KV cache ownership semantics during eviction/rehandoff.

liam: For KMS: do we even allow hosted to mint short-lived guest keys for Private nodes? Compliance wants customer-managed HSM for Private.

anya: Proposal idea: handshake manifest carries a cred_policy field (delegate | customer) and a trusted_proxy flag. Runtime validates a MAC and emits audit events. Keeps control plane small.

maya: Can someone sketch a manifest snippet so we can see the fields together?

sam: Sure, quick example:
```yaml
handshake:
  mode: hosted->private
  cred_policy: delegate
  token_ttl: 120s
  audit: true
```

liam: If cred_policy == delegate, Private must be able to refuse and request rebind. There's a race where rebind + in-flight inference could use stale KV cache entries. Need explicit cache semantics.

anya: We could add cache_isolation: true to the manifest to force a cache flush on handoff, or cache_scope: tenant|session to make it explicit.

maya: Also flagged: dedicated->hosted fallback path when capacity is low. Should we forward customer creds, or swap to a service-account path? Risk: forwarding customer creds increases exposure.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary deploy "probe-handshake-v2" succeeded on runtime-staging at 12:18 UTC :white_check_mark:

sam: For fallback I'd prefer service-account + ephemeral proxy token so we never expose customer KMS to hosted. Add a mapping table to the handshake: fallback_route: service-account | forward-creds.

liam: TL;DR action items: update RFC to include cred_policy matrix, cache_isolation flag, fallback_route enum, and a small state-machine for rebind vs refuse semantics.

maya: I'll update the RFC doc and add a follow-up design note with the state-machine and audit contract. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
